prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Nootaikok, the beneficial Inuit black-dressed spirit dwelling in water inside icebergs and glaciers, leading hunters to seals [nootaikok-c01,c02,c03,c04].
ANATOMY: ONE black-clad spirit suggested by a single fully opaque heavy BLACK HOODED ROBE, one hood/head, two ordinary gloved hands/arms, two legs entirely concealed by long robe, face entirely dark and hidden with NO glowing eyes or invented facial anatomy. Clothing is black throughout [nootaikok-c03]; no crown, antlers, horns, fins, animal head, armor or magical symbols. Humanlike arrangement is only a restrained editorial reading of dressed spirit, not monster anatomy.
MOMENT: UNDERWATER INSIDE an ICEBERG, black-robed spirit sweeps one hand forward to GUIDE three ordinary healthy seals through an existing naturally open blue-ice channel toward a natural daylight opening and waiting adult hunters at ice-edge above [nootaikok-c01,c03,c04]. Other hand braces against ice wall. Spirit fills foreground close to viewer, robe folds float in real water. Friendly dignified guidance, no hunting injury and no hostile face. Clear underwater bubbles, suspended particles, seals swimming, ice ceiling visible overhead establish impossible humanlike presence underwater without breathing apparatus.
POWER: Beneficial offering/guidance of seals [nootaikok-c03,c04] shown ONLY by the open-handed guiding gesture and seals swimming along the way. Glacier walls remain completely stationary, unbroken and untouched: this is an EXISTING NATURAL passage, NOT ice splitting, ice moving or magic. Ordinary gentle underwater current carries small bubbles and moves cloth folds. NO dislodged ice chunks. No light emitted from spirit or robe, no aura.
SCALE & CAMERA: Close low underwater angle, black spirit fills70percent of frame, arms and robe dominate. No invented giant size; seals comparable normal proportions. Distant adult hunters normal size at the above-water opening, no tiny miniatures to suggest giant body.
LIGHT & WEATHER: One dominant shaft of natural low warm sunlight penetrates opening and thick blue glacier ice, black silhouette crisply rimlit by actual transmitted daylight, deep walnut-black cloth shadows. Real water caustics, ice bubbles, no flying ice fragments.
SURFACE: Heavy soaked coarse black robe, scratched dense translucent blue ice, natural slick seal fur, suspended water particles.
SETTING: Interior underwater ice cavern within iceberg/glacier, cold Arctic water, ice-edge opening [nootaikok-c01,c03].
MOOD: overwhelmingly majestic, benevolent guardian dwelling within glacier and guiding seals, active and reverential, never evil, cute or ordinary diver. No swimming equipment.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, logo, border, watermark, nudity, gore, extra limbs/digits, borrowed film/game/anime/comic designs, generic glowing aura, neon outlines, floating runes or energy ribbons.

Three seals swim along offered path toward hunters visible safely above surface. No active ice movement, cracks, flying chunks or magic; water carries ordinary bubbles and cloth. root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and hood, both-hand and hunter crops. What works: one figure dressed entirely in black (nootaikok-c03), legs hidden by the robe, with two black-gloved hands; the guiding hand shows a thumb and four fingers. It is in the water inside a still blue ice channel (c01/c03), guiding three seals toward hunters at the ice edge (c01/c04). No ice magic, aura or text. It fails for two reasons. (1) The hood is an empty black void with no face at all, on a European friar-style robe with flared sleeves and black leather gloves. That is the stock Grim Reaper/Ringwraith/Dementor silhouette, an icon of death and dread, and it turns the documented 'beneficial, friendly spirit' (c03; disposition benevolent, c01) into something sinister. At 200px it reads as a reaper reaching after the seals, not a benevolent spirit offering them. Under §6.5, a benevolent being must stay awe-inspiring and must not be made evil. (2) The three hunters read as bearded European/Siberian trappers in knitted caps and belted coats, not Inuit hunters, so the scene loses the Inuit tradition it illustrates. It fails the tradition-character check and Uji Sangar #7, because it shows the wrong character.

correction_notes: Keep: one spirit dressed in black (nootaikok-c03), in the water inside an iceberg/glacier (c01/c03), guiding seals toward hunters (c01/c03/c04). Keep the ice walls still, with no ice magic or breaking, and no aura or glow. Fix: (a) No void hood. Show a calm, dignified humanlike face, partly shadowed but clearly present, with two eyes and a benevolent expression turned toward the seals or the viewer, so it reads as a friendly guardian spirit. Make the black clothing a heavy hooded Arctic garment of black skin or fur (editorial), not a European friar's robe with flared sleeves and leather gloves. Nothing should read as the Grim Reaper, a Ringwraith or a Dementor. (b) If hunters are shown, they must read as Inuit hunters: fur-ruffed skin parkas and a harpoon, perhaps a kayak at the floe edge. Not bearded European trappers in knitted caps and belted coats. Keep them small and secondary. (c) Keep the majesty: the spirit large and close in the frame, a sweeping offering gesture, seals streaming past it toward the light, and one shaft of daylight through the ice falling on its face. No text.
